insights.question: What is the overall cancellation rate and how much revenue is at risk?
insights.business_relevance: Sizes the core problem in monetary terms; baseline for all mitigation ROI calculations.
insights.finding: 32.76% of 36,275 bookings cancel; EUR 4.30M of EUR 11.35M potential revenue (37.9%) is at risk; average booking value ~EUR 313.
insights.interpretation: Cancellation is not a marginal nuisance: over a third of bookings and nearly 4 of every 10 revenue euros are exposed. Even a partial reduction translates into millions of EUR.
insights.recommended_action: Stand up a cancellation-risk scoring process integrated into the reservation workflow, prioritizing high-value, long-lead bookings.

insights.question: How does lead time affect cancellation probability?
insights.business_relevance: Lead time is the strongest single behavioral driver and defines when interventions should trigger.
insights.interpretation: Long-horizon plans are fragile. Bookings made >6 months ahead cancel at ~7x the rate of last-minute bookings.
insights.recommended_action: Tiered reconfirmation policy by lead-time band; mandatory deposit or non-refundable option for 180+ day bookings.

insights.question: How do market segments differ in cancellation behavior?
insights.business_relevance: Channel-specific risk concentration enables targeted commercial policies.
insights.finding: Online: 36.5% cancel rate on 64% of volume (23,214 bookings). Offline: 29.9%. Aviation: 29.6%. Corporate: 10.9%. Complementary: 0%.
insights.interpretation: The riskiest channel is also the biggest: online OTA-style bookings dominate volume and cancellation risk simultaneously. Corporate bookings are ~3x safer.
insights.recommended_action: For online bookings: require partial prepayment or stricter free-cancellation windows; promote corporate/contracted segments in high season.

insights.question: What is the revenue impact of cancellations by arrival month?
insights.business_relevance: Converts behavior into seasonal financial exposure; tells the business when to act.
insights.finding: Total lost revenue EUR 4.30M; the top-3 loss months concentrate 43.2% of the total loss, driven by peak volume (Aug-Oct) combined with elevated cancellation rates (~35-40%).
insights.interpretation: Seasonal peaks amplify losses: more bookings x high cancel rate = concentrated exposure. October alone carries a disproportionate share.
insights.recommended_action: Apply stricter cancellation terms and proactive overbooking buffers during peak months (Aug-Oct); front-load retention campaigns ahead of them.

insights.question: Do engagement and loyalty signals reduce cancellation probability?
insights.business_relevance: These signals are free, collected at booking time, and highly predictive.
insights.finding: Cancel rate by special requests: 43.2% (0) -> 23.8% (1) -> 14.6% (2) -> 0% (3+). Repeated guests: 1.7% vs 33.6% new guests. Correlation -0.253.
insights.interpretation: Every engagement signal is protective. A booking with zero special requests from a first-time guest is the archetypal high-risk profile.
insights.recommended_action: Nudge guests to add preferences/requests at booking (upsell + retention); prioritize zero-request, first-time, long-lead bookings for reconfirmation.
